page: Amazon Web Services r6idn.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server built on the x86_64 architecture. The platform is powered by Intel Xeon 8375C processors running at a sustained clock speed of 3.5 GHz, providing 64 physical cores and 128 dedicated execution threads. Memory capacity totals 1024 GB of DDR4 operating at 3 GHz, which equates to an allocation of 8 GB per vCPU. The instance bundles 7600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and provides a 200 Gbps baseline network interface. Hardware accelerators such as discrete GPUs are not present on this instance type.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong parallel computing capability and memory performance. The system achieves a top-tier PassMark CPU score of 87984.85, alongside strong multi-core results in stress-ng (124999.69) and Geekbench (17622.0). Memory throughput is sustained at 338.15 GB/sec for large read operations and 133.36 GB/sec for large write operations. In workload tests, the server delivered 107.97 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and registered strong marks in static web serving and database processing. Conversely, single-thread performance benchmarks, such as Geekbench single-core (1682.0) and compression tasks, remain in the middle tier.

By delivering direct bare-metal access without hypervisor virtualization layers, the server provides direct hardware control, cache efficiency, and deterministic latency. The pairing of extensive memory density with 7.6 TB of direct-attached NVMe storage delivers high operational efficiency for consolidated data engines. The principal tradeoff rests on single-thread performance and the lack of GPU hardware, making the instance less cost-effective for serial compute tasks or deep learning model generation.

Amazon Web Services r6idn.metal is suited for memory-bound and I/O-intensive production workloads. Key deployment profiles include large in-memory databases like Redis and Memcached, distributed relational databases, heavy transactional database management systems, big data analytics engines, and high-concurrency batch processing.

Configured with 1024 GB of DDR4 memory, 7600 GB of bundled NVMe SSD storage, and a 200 Gbps network interface, the system eliminates hypervisor overhead while offering an 8 GB RAM per vCPU ratio. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong multi-core computation and high memory bandwidth, achieving 107.97 million Redis SET operations per second and top-tier PassMark cryptographic and CPU scores. While single-thread performance remains average and GPU acceleration is absent, the dense aggregation of memory, fast local storage, and high network throughput makes r6idn.metal highly effective for memory-bound relational databases, in-memory caching tiers, large-scale data analytics, and high-concurrency batch processing workloads.
